title: Out for a Dog Walk
cardDescription: Dog-walking equipment, familiar actions, and simple training words.
description: Head out for a gentle dog-themed crossword about walking equipment, familiar movements, and the simple words heard during play and training.
focus: This puzzle brings together things used on a walk and words describing what a dog does. Some clues ask for equipment or a place, while others ask for an action or a familiar command. Everyday meanings and direct definitions provide the way into the grid.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue describes something worn, something held, a place, or an action. A command can use an ordinary word in a special way. Short movement words can help cross longer names for walking equipment.
words: Strap or cord held to guide a dog on a walk
Band worn around a dog's neck
Set of straps fitted around a dog's body for attaching a lead
Small identification plate attached to a pet's collar
A dog's foot, often leaving a print in soft ground
A mark left on the ground by an animal's foot
To draw air through the nose to investigate a smell
To move a tail from side to side
A dog's steady gait faster than a walk
To go on foot at an ordinary unhurried pace
Public green space where people may walk dogs
Narrow route followed through a park
Movable barrier at the entrance to a fenced area
To go after an object and bring it back
Round toy a dog may chase during play
Small length of wood sometimes carried by a dog
Small food reward offered during dog training
Command asking a dog to walk close beside its handler
Command asking a dog to rest on its haunches
Command asking a dog to remain in place

answerNotes.LEASH: Leash is the common American word for the strap or cord held on a dog walk. Lead is another word for the same item.
answerNotes.COLLAR: A collar goes around the neck. A harness fits around the body, so the location described in the clue distinguishes the equipment.
answerNotes.HARNESS: A harness is an arrangement of body straps. Its position distinguishes it from a collar around the neck, and the clue asks for the whole piece of equipment.
answerNotes.TAG: A tag is a small identification plate in this pet context. It is not the chasing game or the action of labeling something.
answerNotes.PAW: Paw names the animal's foot. Track names a mark left behind, so the body part and its impression are different answers.
answerNotes.FETCH: Fetch means go after something and bring it back. Chasing alone does not include the return described in the clue.
answerNotes.HEEL: Heel is a training command asking for a position close beside the handler. The clue does not use the word for the back part of a human foot.
answerNotes.STAY: Stay is a command to remain where one is. The clue asks for a familiar training word rather than instructions on teaching it.

title: Around the Cat Basket
cardDescription: Young cats, resting places, and everyday household actions.
description: Enjoy a quiet cat-themed crossword about young cats, resting places, and familiar movements and objects around the house.
focus: The clues combine cat vocabulary with resting places, everyday actions, and household objects. Some words name a movement, while others name a place, a body part, or an item used at home. The definitions describe the intended everyday meaning.
solvingTip: Look for whether a clue asks for an action, a resting place, or a household object. A place to rest and the act of resting have different names. Short familiar words can help with longer cat-related answers.
words: Domestic feline commonly kept as a household pet
Long sensory hair on a cat's face
Low vibrating sound a cat may make
Curved pointed nail on a cat's toe
Cat's foot with pads and claws
Long rear appendage a cat may hold upright
Soft body hair covering many cats
A short period of sleep in a sunny spot
Raised resting place from which a cat can look around
Soft padded support inside a pet basket
To scrape a surface with claws
Absorbent material placed in a cat's toilet tray
Shallow open container that can hold cat litter
Round open dish used to serve pet food
Object provided for a cat to play with
To spring suddenly toward a toy or other target
To extend the body and limbs after resting
To clean the coat by licking or brushing

answerNotes.KITTEN: Kitten is the word for a young cat. It identifies an age group rather than one particular breed.
answerNotes.WHISKER: Whiskers are specialized sensory hairs. The clue asks for one hair, so the singular whisker is the form that fits.
answerNotes.PURR: Purr names a low vibrating sound. The clue identifies the sound itself and does not claim that it proves one particular mood.
answerNotes.CLAW: Claw names the curved nail on a toe; paw names the whole foot. The distinction is between a part and the larger body structure.
answerNotes.PERCH: Perch is a raised resting place here. The same spelling also names a fish, but the cat's resting location fixes the household meaning.
answerNotes.LITTER: Litter is the absorbent material in this clue. The word can also name a group of newborn animals, so the reference to a tray distinguishes its use.
answerNotes.POUNCE: Pounce is a sudden spring toward a target. It describes a movement rather than the toy or object being approached.
answerNotes.GROOM: Groom means clean or tend the coat here. It is an action rather than the person at a wedding who has the same name.

title: Small Pets and Their Homes
cardDescription: Small pet names, enclosure words, and familiar movements.
description: Explore the world of small pets with a crossword about familiar mammals, the objects around them, and the ways they move.
focus: This puzzle combines small mammal names with words for homes, food, and movement. Clues describe familiar features or uses rather than asking for breed knowledge. The setting helps distinguish everyday words with more than one meaning.
solvingTip: Notice whether the answer names an animal, a home, or a movement. A dwelling dug underground and a structure built above ground have different names. Use familiar short words before working on the longer animal or enclosure terms.
words: Small pet rodent known for expandable cheek pouches
Long-eared mammal that often moves by hopping
Small long-tailed rodent often kept as a pet
Another name for a guinea pig
Small rodent whose plural is mice
Long-tailed rodent generally larger than a mouse
Raised or enclosed shelter traditionally associated with rabbits
Enclosure with bars or wire sides
Material lining the floor of a small pet's enclosure
Tunnel or underground home dug by an animal
Enclosed passage a small pet may move through
To go out of sight inside a shelter
Dried grasses or other forage eaten by pet rabbits
Small compressed piece of prepared pet food

To bite repeatedly at something with the front teeth
Round exercise device a hamster can run inside
Cozy resting structure made from gathered material
Hair covering the body of a rabbit or hamster
To move with a short springing jump

answerNotes.HAMSTER: Hamsters have cheek pouches used to carry food or other material. The clue uses that recognizable feature rather than naming a particular variety.
answerNotes.CAVY: Cavy is another name for the guinea pig. It is a vocabulary alternative for the familiar pet rather than a different breed.
answerNotes.MOUSE: Mouse has the irregular plural mice. The clue refers to the animal rather than a computer pointing device.
answerNotes.HUTCH: Hutch is a shelter word often associated with rabbits. It can also name a piece of household furniture, but the animal context fixes this meaning.
answerNotes.BEDDING: Bedding names material in an enclosure here. It does not refer to a complete enclosure or identify one recommended material.
answerNotes.BURROW: A burrow is a tunnel or underground dwelling made by an animal. Borrow has a different spelling and meaning despite looking similar.
answerNotes.PELLET: Pellet describes a small compressed piece. The clue uses the word for a food form without specifying a feeding amount or diet.
answerNotes.GNAW: Gnaw begins with a silent g in ordinary American pronunciation. The clue describes repeated biting with the front teeth.
answerNotes.WHEEL: Wheel names the round exercise device here. The clue describes an object rather than specifying a size or a care routine.

title: Feathered Pet Friends
cardDescription: Familiar pet birds, their body parts, and the sounds they make.
description: Meet some feathered companions through a crossword about familiar pet birds, their body parts, and the sounds and actions associated with them.
focus: The clues cover bird names, visible features, sounds, and a few objects in a bird's surroundings. Some words have broader everyday meanings. The definitions identify their bird-related use without requiring an identification guide.
solvingTip: Check whether a clue names a kind of bird, one body part, an object, or an action. A hard mouthpart and a feathered forelimb have different names. Use the short sound and action clues to help cross longer bird-related words.
words: Hook-billed bird, some kinds of which can imitate human speech
Small pet songbird often associated with yellow feathers
Small seed-eating bird with a short stout beak
Short name for a budgerigar, a small pet parakeet
Small Australian parrot with a prominent head crest
Bird often associated with a soft cooing call
One of the lightweight structures covering a bird's body
Feathered forelimb a bird uses for flight
Sharp curved claw on a bird's foot
Rod or branch on which a pet bird rests
Barred enclosure often pictured as a pet bird's home
Large enclosure in which birds can fly
Small plant structure eaten by many pet birds
Small-seeded cereal often offered to birds in sprays
To make a short high-pitched bird sound
Short light call made by a small bird
To produce a sequence of musical bird sounds
To imitate a heard sound, as some parrots do
To clean and arrange feathers with the beak

answerNotes.PARROT: Parrots are known for curved beaks, and some can imitate sounds or speech. That ability is not a promise about every individual bird.
answerNotes.CANARY: Canaries are familiar pet songbirds. Yellow is a well-known color, but canaries also have other colors, so the clue says often associated.
answerNotes.BUDGIE: Budgie is short for budgerigar, a small parakeet. Parakeet is a broader name that can refer to other kinds of birds as well.
answerNotes.COCKATIEL: A cockatiel is an Australian parrot with a recognizable crest. The head feature distinguishes it from a bird name based only on color.
answerNotes.FEATHER: A feather is one structure in a bird's covering. A wing is a whole forelimb that carries many feathers.
answerNotes.PERCH: Perch is a resting rod or branch here. The spelling also names a fish, so the described object selects the bird-related meaning.
answerNotes.AVIARY: An aviary is an enclosure with space for birds to fly. It names the structure rather than a particular bird species.
answerNotes.MIMIC: Mimic means imitate a sound in this clue. It describes an action and does not require every parrot to perform it.
answerNotes.PREEN: Preening involves cleaning and arranging feathers with the beak. The word is used for feather care here, although preen can also describe a person taking pride in their appearance.

title: Life in a Fish Tank
cardDescription: Fish, their body parts, and familiar aquarium objects.
description: Look into a fish tank through an easy crossword about familiar aquarium fish, their body parts, and the objects around them.
focus: This puzzle brings together fish names, swimming vocabulary, and familiar aquarium objects. Clues distinguish parts of a fish from parts of its surroundings. Everyday words may have a particular meaning in this watery setting.
solvingTip: Decide whether a clue asks for a fish, a body part, a food form, or an object in the tank. A small plate covering a fish and small stones covering the bottom have different names. Short familiar words can help with longer fish or equipment names.
words: Container commonly made of glass to hold pet fish
Water-filled enclosure for displaying fish or other aquatic life
Common pet fish often pictured as orange or golden
Small aquarium fish whose females give birth to live young
Small schooling aquarium fish, as in the neon variety
Thin projecting body part used by a fish for movement or balance
Breathing organ through which a fish takes oxygen from water
One of the small overlapping plates on many fish
Rear part of a fish that helps propel it through water
Device that removes material from aquarium water as it passes through
Device that moves air or water in an aquarium
Small stones used to cover the bottom of a fish tank
Living greenery that may grow in an aquarium
Simple photosynthetic organisms that may form a coating in a tank
Transparent material used for many aquarium walls
Mesh tool used to lift or transfer aquarium fish
Thin dry piece of prepared fish food
To move through water using body movements
Group of fish swimming together in a coordinated way

answerNotes.AQUARIUM: An aquarium is an enclosure for aquatic life. The same word can also name a public place with many such displays.
answerNotes.GOLDFISH: Goldfish occur in more colors than gold or orange. The clue uses a familiar pictured appearance rather than a rule for every fish.
answerNotes.GUPPY: Guppies give birth to live young. The clue uses that reproductive feature to distinguish the name without relying only on color.
answerNotes.GILL: A gill is a breathing organ; gills is the plural. The singular wording in the clue asks for one organ.
answerNotes.SCALE: Scale names one small plate in a fish's body covering here. It does not mean a weighing device or a set of musical notes.
answerNotes.FILTER: Filter names a device through which water passes to remove material. Pump names a device that moves air or water, which is a different function.
answerNotes.ALGAE: Algae is the usual plural of alga. The word covers diverse photosynthetic organisms and does not name just one aquarium plant.
answerNotes.NET: Net is a mesh tool in this clue. Its openings let water pass through while the tool can hold a fish.
answerNotes.SCHOOL: School describes fish moving together in a coordinated group. It is not a building for lessons in this watery context.
